parts.headline: AI Spending Has Met Its First Real Bill
The Model Is Not the Price

mentions.excerpt: Warden Capital’s second-quarter letter starts at the top.
Warden Capital, on July 22, put the model providers' required end revenue near $1 trillion by 2029 on roughly $700 billion a year of investment.

sides.claim: Warden Capital argues the AI investment cycle cannot earn a reasonable return absent AGI within a few years: at roughly $700 billion per year of investment, model providers would need about $1 trillion in annual end AI revenue by 2029, ramping…

Warden Capital says they are relatively confident the AI boom ends in a bust but do not know when, are not certain it causes a US recession, and cannot judge how deep one would be; they add that the debt-heavy neocloud and datacenter financing…
